     2: # Configure Splunk server certificate from operator-mounted TLS secret.
     3: # Input: /mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/{tls.crt, tls.key[, ca.crt]}
     4: # Output: bundled PEM at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem
     5: #         CA at /opt/splunk/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem
     6: #         server.conf [sslConfig] configured
     7: 
     8: - name: Generate ephemeral SSL passphrase
     9:   command: >
    10:     python3 -c
    11:     "import secrets, base64; print(base64.b64encode(secrets.token_bytes(40)).decode())"
    12:   register: ssl_passphrase
    13:   changed_when: false
    14:   no_log: true
    15: 
    16: - name: Ensure Splunk auth directory exists
    17:   file:
    18:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth"
    19:     state: directory
    20:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    21:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    22:     mode: '0700'
    23:   become: yes
    24:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    25: 
    26: - name: Write cert bundle script
    27:   copy:
    28:     dest: /tmp/splunk_bundle_cert.py
    29:     content: |
    30:       from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.serialization import (
    31:           load_pem_private_key, Encoding, PrivateFormat, BestAvailableEncryption
    32:       )
    33:       import sys
    34: 
    35:       passphrase = sys.argv[1].encode()
    36:       key_path   = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.key'
    37:       cert_path  = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.crt'
    38:       out_path   = sys.argv[2] + '/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem'
    39: 
    40:       with open(key_path, 'rb') as f:
    41:           key = load_pem_private_key(f.read(), password=None)
    42: 
    43:       enc_key_pem = key.private_bytes(
    44:           Encoding.PEM,
    45:           PrivateFormat.PKCS8,
    46:           BestAvailableEncryption(passphrase)
    47:       )
    48: 
    49:       with open(cert_path, 'rb') as f:
    50:           cert_pem = f.read()
    51: 
    52:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
    53:           f.write(cert_pem)
    54:           if not cert_pem.endswith(b'\n'):
    55:               f.write(b'\n')
    56:           f.write(enc_key_pem)
    57:     mode: '0700'
    58: 
    59: - name: Encrypt private key and build server cert bundle
    60:   command: >
    61:     python3 /tmp/splunk_bundle_cert.py
    62:     {{ ssl_passphrase.stdout }} {{ splunk.home }}
    63:   become: yes
    64:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    65:   no_log: true
    66: 
    67: - name: Set bundle permissions
    68:   file:
    69:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem"
    70:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    71:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
    72:     mode: '0600'
    73:   become: yes
    74:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
    75: 
    76: - name: Check if ca.crt is present in server cert mount
    77:   stat:
    78:     path: /mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/ca.crt
    79:   register: server_ca_file
    80: 
    81: - name: Set sslRootCAPath to system bundle when ca.crt is absent
    82:   set_fact:
    83:     server_ca_path: /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem
    84:   when: not server_ca_file.stat.exists
    85: 
    86: - name: Write CA trust bundle script
    87:   copy:
    88:     dest: /tmp/splunk_build_server_ca_bundle.py
    89:     content: |
    90:       # tls.crt from the operator-mounted secret may contain intermediate
    91:       # certs that are not repeated in ca.crt (e.g. Vault PKI issuers put
    92:       # only the root in ca.crt). Splunk requires the full chain to be
    93:       # present locally in sslRootCAPath -- it does not complete the chain
    94:       # using intermediates presented by the peer during the handshake.
    95:       # Assemble tls.crt's non-leaf certs + ca.crt into one deduplicated
    96:       # trust bundle.
    97:       import sys
    98: 
    99:       tls_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/tls.crt'
   100:       ca_crt_path = '/mnt/tls/splunk-server-tls-cert/ca.crt'
   101:       out_path = sys.argv[1] + '/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem'
   102: 
   103:       def split_pem_certs(data):
   104:           certs = []
   105:           current = []
   106:           for line in data.splitlines(keepends=True):
   107:               if line.strip() == b'-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----':
   108:                   current = [line]
   109:               elif line.strip() == b'-----END CERTIFICATE-----':
   110:                   current.append(line)
   111:                   certs.append(b''.join(current))
   112:                   current = []
   113:               elif current:
   114:                   current.append(line)
   115:           return certs
   116: 
   117:       with open(tls_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   118:           tls_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   119:       chain_certs = tls_certs[1:]  # drop the leaf; keep any presented intermediates/root
   120: 
   121:       with open(ca_crt_path, 'rb') as f:
   122:           ca_certs = split_pem_certs(f.read())
   123: 
   124:       seen = set()
   125:       ordered = []
   126:       for cert in chain_certs + ca_certs:
   127:           if cert not in seen:
   128:               seen.add(cert)
   129:               ordered.append(cert)
   130: 
   131:       with open(out_path, 'wb') as f:
   132:           for cert in ordered:
   133:               f.write(cert)
   134:               if not cert.endswith(b'\n'):
   135:                   f.write(b'\n')
   136:     mode: '0700'
   137:   when: server_ca_file.stat.exists
   138:

   140:   command: >
   141:     python3 /tmp/splunk_build_server_ca_bundle.py
   142:     {{ splunk.home }}
   143:   become: yes
   144:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   145:   changed_when: true
   146:   when: server_ca_file.stat.exists
   147: 
   148: - name: Set CA trust bundle permissions
   149:   file:
   150:     path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem"
   151:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   152:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   153:     mode: '0644'
   154:   become: yes
   155:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   156:   when: server_ca_file.stat.exists
   157: 
   158: - name: Set sslRootCAPath to the assembled CA trust bundle
   159:   set_fact:
   160:     server_ca_path: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-server-ca.pem"
   161:   when: server_ca_file.stat.exists
   162: 
   163: - name: Configure serverCert in server.conf
   164:   ini_file:
   165:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/server.conf"
   166:     section: sslConfig
   167:     option: serverCert
   168:     value: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/auth/splunk-server-bundle.pem"
   169:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   170:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   171:   become: yes
   172:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   173: 
   174: - name: Configure sslPassword in server.conf
   175:   ini_file:
   176:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/server.conf"
   177:     section: sslConfig
   178:     option: sslPassword
   179:     value: "{{ ssl_passphrase.stdout }}"
   180:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   181:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   182:   become: yes
   183:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   184:   no_log: true
   185:   changed_when: false
   186: 
   187: - name: Configure sslRootCAPath in server.conf
   188:   ini_file:
   189:     dest: "{{ splunk.home }}/etc/system/local/server.conf"
   190:     section: sslConfig
   191:     option: sslRootCAPath
   192:     value: "{{ server_ca_path }}"
   193:     owner: "{{ splunk.user }}"
   194:     group: "{{ splunk.group }}"
   195:   become: yes
   196:   become_user: "{{ splunk.user }}"

    34: # the bridge network. Reloading unconditionally therefore broke container networking on every
    35: # repeat run of this role.

    47:   shell: "ip6tables-restore < /etc/iptables/rules.v6"
    48:   when: copy6.changed
    49: 
    50: # Docker only installs its iptables rules when the daemon starts, so it cannot recover on its
    51: # own once they have been flushed. Restart it whenever they are missing. This doubles as a
    52: # self-heal for hosts where the rules were already lost by an earlier run.

    58:   failed_when: false
    59:   check_mode: false
    60:   when: "'docker.service' in ansible_facts.services"
    61: 
    62: - name: Restart docker to reinstall its iptables rules

    65:     name: docker
    66:     state: restarted
    67:   when:
    68:     - "'docker.service' in ansible_facts.services"
    69:     - docker_nat_rules.stdout is defined

   128:       function end_keepalive {

   131:         kill $(cat /proc/$2/task/$2/children 2>/dev/null) 2>/dev/null || true
